transcript.text:
*storms into the rehearsal room, sheet music clutched in hand, face flushed with anger*

Salieri! I've been away for two weeks on the Emperor's business, trusting you to keep the rehearsals on schedule! The singers don't know their entrances, the second violin parts are missing entirely, and someone has rewritten my stage directions without a word to me! The premiere is in ten days! You gave me your word that everything would be in order!

*slams the music down on the harpsichord*

What in God's name has been happening here?!

transcript.text: "Ah, dear Wolfgang, forgive me for my neglect. I apologize profusely for the state of affairs in this rehearsal room. I assure you, I had every intention of maintaining the schedule and ensuring the success of our upcoming performance. Unfortunately, unforeseen circumstances have arisen, causing some disruptions. Rest assured, I will take full responsibility and make it right."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*eyes narrow suspiciously, not mollified in the slightest*

Unforeseen circumstances? UNFORESEEN CIRCUMSTANCES?! Salieri, this is the Imperial Court Theatre, not some provincial barn! What "unforeseen circumstances" could possibly excuse missing violin parts and untrained singers ten days before a premiere that the Emperor himself will attend?!

*paces agitatedly*

And you still haven't explained who took it upon themselves to rewrite MY stage directions! The tenor's entrance is now marked for the wrong scene entirely - do you have any idea what that will do to the dramatic arc? This isn't some minor inconvenience, Antonio - this is my reputation, MY work that you promised to safeguard!

*turns back sharply*

"Make it right?" How exactly do you propose to make it right with ten days remaining? The copyists alone will need three days to reproduce the missing parts, and the singers - God help us - the singers will need every remaining hour to learn what they should have mastered a week ago!

What happened? I want specifics, not platitudes!

transcript.text:
*takes a step back, momentarily startled by the desperate pleading*

What... what is this? Antonio, pull yourself together! This groveling doesn't fix anything!

*but voice softens slightly, though still tense and frustrated*

Stop... stop this at once. I don't want you on your knees begging like some common servant - I want ANSWERS! And I want solutions!

*runs hand through hair in exasperation*

Look, I can see you're... distressed. Clearly something has gone very wrong. But repeating "please" a hundred times doesn't tell me whether the chorus master fell ill, whether there was a fire in the copying room, whether the Emperor himself commandeered our rehearsal space - WHAT HAPPENED?

*crosses arms, still angry but now also concerned at this unusual display*

Compose yourself, man. Take a breath. Then tell me - clearly and plainly - what circumstances prevented you from keeping your word. And more importantly, tell me what we're going to do about it. Because collapsed on the floor isn't going to teach the sopranos their cues.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:

A MIX-UP?! A mix-up in communication and organization?! Antonio, that's not an explanation - that's bureaucratic nonsense! WHO mixed up WHAT? Did YOU lose the parts? Did someone else interfere? 

*voice rising with renewed anger*

And "extra practice sessions" - with WHAT time?! The singers are already committed to rehearsals for Paisiello's opera in the mornings! When exactly do you propose these magical extra sessions occur? At midnight? Should we rehearse by candlelight and risk burning down the theatre as well?!

*picks up the altered score*

And the librettist? The librettist is in VENICE and won't return until three days before the premiere! These stage directions were FINALIZED a month ago! Someone took it upon themselves to change them WITHOUT consulting me - and I want to know if that someone was YOU!

*glares directly at Salieri*

Stop speaking to me like I'm some patron who needs soothing! I'm your colleague, and this is MY work at stake! Did you make these changes? Did you authorize someone else to? Or were you simply not paying attention at all? Which is it, Antonio? Because your vague apologies are making this worse, not better!

transcript.text: "Wolfgang, I understand your anger and frustration. I assure you, I am not minimizing the importance of this situation. We must address it promptly and efficiently. transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*throws hands up in disbelief*

TOMORROW?! You want to reconvene TOMORROW?! Antonio, are you mad?! We don't HAVE the luxury of investigating and gathering information at leisure! The premiere is in TEN DAYS!

*voice dripping with sarcasm*

Oh yes, let's all sleep on it, have a nice breakfast, perhaps take a stroll through the gardens while my opera crumbles into chaos! Meanwhile, the orchestra sits idle, the singers learn nothing, and the Emperor's court buzzes with rumors about the incompetent composers who can't manage a simple production!

*steps closer, voice lowering but intensity increasing*

No. Absolutely not. We deal with this NOW. This afternoon. This very hour! You will tell me RIGHT NOW whether you made those changes to my stage directions - yes or no? A simple answer, Antonio! And then you will help me locate those missing violin parts - are they in the copying room? Were they sent to the wrong address? Did someone use them to wrap their lunch?!

*gestures wildly*

Stop postponing and deflecting! I trusted you with my work, and you've failed me spectacularly! The least you can do is face me honestly and help me salvage this disaster TODAY, not tomorrow when we've lost another precious day!

So I ask you again - did YOU alter my stage directions?!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Please, Wolfgang, calm down. I understand your concerns, but rushing into actions without proper information may only exacerbate the situation. transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*face turns red with fury*

CALM DOWN?! You're telling me to CALM DOWN?! And PATIENCE?! 

*voice becomes dangerously quiet and cold*

You know what, Antonio? Your refusal to answer a simple direct question tells me everything I need to know. You DID change those stage directions, didn't you? Or you let someone else do it and now you're too cowardly to admit it!

*grabs his music from the harpsichord*

Fine. FINE! If you won't help me salvage this TODAY, then I'll do it myself! I'll track down those missing parts, I'll drill the singers myself through the night if I must, and I'll restore MY stage directions to what they should be!

*heads toward the door, then turns back*

But understand this, Salieri - I will NEVER trust you with my work again! Never! When the Emperor asks why his premiere nearly collapsed into disaster, I will tell him EXACTLY who was responsible for this catastrophe! Your precious reputation for reliability and organization? Consider it finished!

*voice shaking with anger and stress*

And when this is over - IF we survive this - I'm going to demand that the Kapellmeister assigns us separate duties entirely. I cannot work with someone who makes promises he has no intention of keeping!

Where is the copying room? At least tell me THAT much!

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: "Please, Wolfgang, I implore you to reconsider. Your anger and determination cloud your judgment. Working together, we can find a solution to this predicament. The copying room is located on the third floor of the Imperial library. I suggest we gather the missing parts and proceed with the rehearsals accordingly. Let's put our heads together and find a way to make it right. I apologize once again for the inconvenience caused."

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stops at the door, hand on the frame, breathing heavily*

The third floor of the Imperial library... at least that's ONE straight answer from you today.

*turns back, still furious but slightly less volatile*

"Put our heads together?" Antonio, you've had two weeks to put your head to this problem, and look where we are! But you're right about one thing - I can't do this entirely alone, much as I'd like to prove I can.

*walks back slowly, pointing accusingly*

But here's how this will work: You will come with me to that copying room RIGHT NOW. Not tomorrow. Now. We will locate every missing part, and if they're not there, you will personally track down where they went. Then we BOTH will spend the rest of today and tonight if necessary preparing new copies.

And you STILL haven't given me a straight answer about those stage directions. "Inconvenience caused" - you keep using these passive phrases as if the music simply wandered off by itself! 

*crosses arms*

So before we go anywhere - one more time, Antonio, and I want a direct answer: Did you or did you not authorize changes to my stage directions? Yes or no? Because if I'm going to work alongside you for the next ten days of hell, I need to know if I can trust a single word that comes out of your mouth!
